analysis.title: USA: Core CPI Above Expectations; Estimating 0.35% for October Core PCE
key_insights: Core CPI rose 0.30% month-over-month in October, above the median forecast of +0.2% and GS's +0.16%. The surprise came from firmer readings across a broad set of categories.

Owners' equivalent rent (OER) rose 0.32% month-over-month, firm for the second consecutive month. The strength was concentrated in the Midwest (+0.4%, seasonally adjusted by GS). Rent rose a softer 0.20%.
Medical services rose 0.3% month-over-month despite a decline in health insurance prices after the BLS incorporated updated source data on insurance premiums.
Motor vehicle insurance prices rebounded 0.7% month-over-month after running softer this year. Travel services stayed firm, with hotels +0.7% and airfares +0.4%.
Headline CPI rose 0.35% month-over-month, above the median forecast of +0.3% and GS's +0.21%. Energy prices rose 0.7%, which GS attributes to the re-escalation of the conflict in Iran.
Year-over-year CPI figures are not available this month because October 2025 values are missing, due to last year's government shutdown disrupting data collection.
From the CPI details, GS estimates October core PCE rose 0.35% month-over-month, versus its 0.23% expectation before the CPI release. That implies +3.30% year-over-year.
GS expects October headline PCE rose 0.36% month-over-month and 3.87% from a year earlier.

risk_factors: Year-over-year CPI cannot be calculated for October because of missing October 2025 data from last year's government shutdown, which makes the inflation trend harder to read.
The health insurance premium data update lowered insurance prices, which may distort the medical category in coming prints.
geopolitical: Re-escalation of the conflict in Iran raised energy prices, with energy CPI up 0.7% in October.
